podcast.body: Tears for Fears' 1982 single, which featured lyrically dark themes but was characterized by pinging synthesizers and a driving, "pepier" tempo. Twenty years later, it was famously covered by Michael Andrews and Gary Jules for the "Donnie Darko" soundtrack, reimagined as a spooky, slowed-down "bummer cover." "Tears for Fear's 1982 single Mad World."

podcast.body: This single was released in Fall 1982 (September) and became an "across the board hit," popular in new wave, alternative rock, and pop genres. Roland Orzabal wrote the song, with Curt Smith, the bass player, performing the vocals. "A single called Mad World was released the previous fall. This would be September 1982. And it became an across the board hit."
